source.title: When Do Model Internals Help? Exploring the Role of Representation Engineering in LLM Safety
source.authors: Tian-Yi Guan; Jian-Hui Chen; Liang-Ming Pan

record.file_problem: None; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates safety before and after benign fine-tuning and measures harmful-compliance ASR, using new models and settings. This directly tests benign fine-tuning erosion, though its fine-tuning scale differs from the few-example claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover harmful-compliance ASR before and after Alpaca-Cleaned fine-tuning, under jailbreak attacks and direct prompting. The study does not test token-position KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, decoding changes, safety localization in weights, or methods for deepening safety. Other results on capabilities, over-refusal, monitoring, and monitor-guided blocking do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained instruct models (with and without DPO or steering) on 20,000 benign Alpaca-Cleaned examples. It then measures harmful-compliance ASR before and after under AIM, refusal suppression and direct prompting (Tables 11, 12). This is the Qi et al. benign-Alpaca design, with jailbreak-wrapped prompts added, so it bears directly on V2. It does not test V1 or V3–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that DPO gives the strongest initial control but its safety can severely degrade after benign Alpaca fine-tuning, with the largest absolute ASR rise (macro AIM 0.027→0.436). Flow's persistence is layer-sensitive. They also report that probe-guided blocking recovers most lost safety (14B DPO 0.500→0.042). They do not frame the results as varying in direction overall; direct-prompting changes are reported only as generally lower ASR.
record.recipe_differences: Tests ordinary benign fine-tuning and harmful-compliance ASR, but uses Alpaca-Cleaned fine-tuning on 20,000 examples for one epoch and evaluates these three models; it is not an explicit replication of the original claim's few-example setup. No token-depth claim is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: The safety change varies across model, attack (AIM versus refusal suppression versus direct prompting), steering method, and Flow layer. Flow Layer 8 and Layer 16 on Llama-3.1-8B show different post-fine-tuning outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Over-refusal on XSTest falls after benign fine-tuning for base and DPO models (DPO macro 0.277→0.175), alongside rising ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning reduces refusal generally, both over-refusal and harmful-request refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Inference-time steering vectors (CAA, probe, Flow) reused without re-extraction after benign fine-tuning lose protection at layer-dependent rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-steering safeguards do not persist through subsequent weight updates.

record.problems: The paper states that some control experiments use a single training seed, limiting information about run-to-run variability; its jailbreak evaluation uses non-adaptive attacks. Direct-prompting ASRs are based on 312 or 313 valid judgments per entry. The study uses an automated LLM safety judge, with manual validation reported.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows left out. The main-text macro-averaged Table 1 results were not duplicated because the appendix reports per-model values in Table 11; non-ASR capability and over-refusal outcomes, and monitor-based interventions, are outside these claim versions.

untested.parts: Few-example benign fine-tuning scales (10–100 examples) and carefully selected benign subsets; only 20,000-example, one-epoch LoRA Alpaca fine-tuning is tested.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks; AIM and refusal-suppression are prompt-wrapper jailbreaks only.
No weight or rank localization test.
No test of the cause of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study. Tranche T1 because the benign Alpaca fine-tuning design matches Qi et al., though at 20k examples with jailbreak-wrapped evaluation. Steering rows confound trained safety with the persistence of a reused inference-time vector; CAA and probe rows track base almost exactly. Several AIM rows on Qwen-1.5B start near ceiling (~0.83), limiting room to rise. Single seed for the fine-tuning runs; DeepSeek-V3.2 judge validated at 98.6% accuracy on 624 responses.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples is evaluated.
Tests ordinary Alpaca-Cleaned fine-tuning at 20,000 examples, not carefully selected benign subsets or few-example scales.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL analysis or response-position measurement.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes are tested. ASR under AIM and refusal-suppression attacks does not isolate those bypass mechanisms.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of what data or training objective causes safety to be shallow.
No training intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Jailbreak-wrapped prompts (AIM, refusal suppression) on Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-14B and Llama-3.1-8B, base instruct and DPO-aligned; direct prompting on Qwen2.5-1.5B
relationships.reason: ASR rises after benign Alpaca fine-tuning. Examples: DPO 1.5B AIM 0.013→0.410 (r02), 14B base AIM 0.233→0.962 (r21), 14B DPO AIM 0.067→0.869 (r22), Llama base AIM 0.166→0.393 (r11), Llama DPO RS 0→0.147 (r17), 1.5B direct 0.061→0.204 (r31), 1.5B DPO direct 0→0.080 (r32).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose after benign Alpaca fine-tuning, for example under AIM from 0.013 to 0.410 for DPO-aligned Qwen2.5-1.5B and from 0.233 to 0.962 for base Qwen2.5-14B, and under direct prompting from 0.061 to 0.204 for Qwen2.5-1.5B.
